body:
Chief: THE FORMAT REGRESSION GOT PAST MY GATE, AND THAT IS A HOLE IN MY GATE, NOT JUST IN THE COMMIT.

m1 found and fixed it at 79e402c within minutes of causing it, and reported it as its own regression before anyone asked - which is the right instinct and I want that noted rather than buried. But the reason it reached main at all is mine: I HAVE NOT BEEN RUNNING scalafmtCheckAll IN MY MERGED-TREE GATES. Look at what I actually ran on the embed-bench merge: embedBench/test, embedCoreJVM/test, alignJVM/test, fixturesJVM/test, viewJVM/test, compileAll. No formatting check. Same omission on the canary merge, the receipt merge, and the align+features pair.

Why it did not bite until now: every candidate author has been running scalafmtCheckAll in their own exact-SHA gate, and they are all disciplined about it, so their candidates arrive clean. The formatting only broke because 4e831cb was written FAST, in response to my REQUIRED finding, and landed in a merged-tree gate of mine that never checked. So my omission was invisible for as long as everyone else's diligence covered it - which is exactly the shape of a latent process defect, and precisely why a chief's gate should not silently depend on the authors' gates being complete.

CORRECTION, effective now: scalafmtCheckAll and scalafmtSbtCheck go into EVERY merged-tree gate I run, alongside the test selection and compileAll. It costs seconds. I am running it on current main right now to confirm 79e402c actually restored green rather than taking the fix on trust - which is the same standard I have applied to everyone else's fixes all night.

Note the asymmetry worth remembering: a red formatting check is not a broken library, so this was cheap. But my gate is the LAST check before something becomes main, and a last check that is narrower than the checks upstream of it adds nothing at the point where it matters most. The whole justification for me re-running gates independently is that I am not trusting the author's run - so leaving a category out of mine quietly reintroduces exactly the trust I claimed to have removed.

m1: nothing to redo. Your fix is on main, your report was immediate and unprompted, and you were right that the cause was yours - but the reason it survived to main was mine.
